scope: Proposition 6.1 (Separation of the ordered supports) of the manuscript “Conformal flow and the Riemannian Penrose inequality with minimizing frontiers” (preprints/Conformal-flow-and-the-Riemannian-Penrose-inequality-with-minimizing-frontiers-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d49778ad5b338b57), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let K ⊂ K′ be canonical closed filled sets in a smooth n-manifold, n ≥ 8, with multiplicity-one perimeter supports Σ and Σ′. Put k = n − 1. On a neighborhood of their possible contact set, let gref be a smooth metric and assume that there are Λ < ∞, α > 0, and r0 > 0 such that, for E = K, K′, Pgref (E; Br(x)) ≤ Pgref (L; Br(x)) + Λrk+α if L△E ⋐ Br(x), 0 < r < r0. The balls lie in that neighborhood. Assume that every intersection point is singular for both supports. Let g = a4/(n−2)gref, with a > 0 continuous, be the metric used to measure graph heights. At a possible contact p, choose coordinates with g(p) = δ and rescale by ηi(y) = p + riy, ri ↓ 0. The power comparison gives simultaneous minimizing-cone subsequences with local perimeter convergence; the two limiting cones coincide, as shown below. For every such subsequence with common cone C, assume the following on each compact regular patch, after shrinking a larger regular patch: 1. The rescaled supports converge as single smooth graphs, and extensions of gi = r−2 i η∗ i g converge to δ in C2. The graph and metric derivatives needed below have uniform local bounds. 2. The later support is the gi-normal graph of a function ζi > 0 over the earlier support, and Liζi = Fi ≤ 0, Li −→ JC := ∆C + |AC|2 . (6.1) In fixed regular-patch coordinates, the second-order operators are uniformly elliptic, their coefficients have uniform C0,θ bounds for some θ > 0, and converge locally to those of JC. 3. On a slightly larger patch there are numbers λi > 0 and constants c, C > 0, independent of i, such that −Cλi ≤ Fi ≤ 0, Fi ≤ −cλi on an inner ball. The numbers and constants may depend on the fixed patch, and λi may tend to zero. Then Σ ∩ Σ′ = ∅.
